appraisal_events.evidence: Morel qui était au bureau de la presse et dont personne ne connaissait la situation irrégulière affectait de trouver, son sang français bouillant dans ses veines comme le jus des raisins de Combray, que c'était peu de chose que d'être dans un bureau pendant la guerre et feignait de vouloir s'engager (alors qu'il n'avait qu'à rejoindre)
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator exposes Morel's hypocritical posturing: he affects patriotic indignation and feigns wanting to enlist while concealing his irregular exempt status, deflating his self-presentation.

appraisal_events.evidence: Cottard assistait maintenant aux réceptions dans un uniforme de colonel de « l'île du Rêve », assez semblable à celui d'un amiral haïtien [...] Cottard mourut bientôt « face à l'ennemi », dirent les journaux, bien qu'il n'eût pas quitté Paris, mais se fût, en effet, surmené pour son âge
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator mocks Cottard's absurd fictitious military costume and notes the irony that the papers reported him dying 'facing the enemy' though he never left Paris, undercutting the heroic narrative even while acknowledging his real, unglamorous exhaustion.

appraisal_events.evidence: M. Verdurin, dont la mort chagrina une seule personne qui fut, le croirait-on, Elstir [...] n'avaient pas comme Swann, comme M. Verdurin, reçu des leçons de goût de Whistler, des leçons de vérité de Monet, leur permettant de juger Elstir avec justice
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator notes with irony that M. Verdurin's death grieved almost no one except Elstir, who alone had the trained taste to judge his art justly and mourn him as a genuine connoisseur, combining broad social insignificance with a narrow, authentic prestige.

status_effects.explanation: Morel's feigned patriotism and concealed irregular exemption cast him as a hypocrite in the narrator's ironic exposition.

His ridiculous costume and the gap between the papers' heroic account and mundane truth deflate his self-important public image, though his real exhaustion lends a touch of genuine, unglamorous sacrifice.
Despite decades hosting a salon, his death draws grief from almost no one, revealing limited genuine attachment to him.
Elstir's singular, genuine grief and the praise of his Whistler/Monet-trained taste grant him a narrow but authentic form of esteem as a true connoisseur.

ambiguities: Mme Verdurin's indignation that M. de Cambremer, despite his age, held a staff post ('à son âge, fût dans un état-major') was read as continuous with her already-scored pattern of doubting absentees' service rather than a distinct new movement, so M. de Cambremer was not scored separately; a stricter reading might treat this as a direct discrediting of him.

Elstir's extended reflection on M. Verdurin's death (his sense of isolation, the loss of a witness to his art's authenticity) was treated as evidence supporting M. Verdurin's mixed status rather than scored as its own event targeting Elstir, since the passage reads primarily as essayistic reflection on art; a less conservative reading might score Elstir's personal emotional loss separately.
